subject: Clarify: June pilot invoice reconciliation — token accounting, context & minimums
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@swiftretail.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: billing@swiftretail.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Question on June pilot invoice — rounding and long-context requests

Hi Grace / Jordan,

We received the invoice for our June pilot and have a couple of items we need clarified before we submit payment:

- Line item 3 shows 1,240 "token units" billed but our internal logs show ~1,010 model tokens consumed. Can you explain how the token units map to the raw model tokens?
- There appears to be a surge billing at 14:35 PDT on 6/21 for very long chat sessions — are these being bucketed differently because of the 64k context handling?
- Lastly, the invoice rounds to the nearest 100 token units for several microcalls. Is there a minimum per-call floor applied?

Attaching the invoice PDF we received. If possible, could you provide a short worked example that maps the invoice rows back to raw tokens and context lengths? We need this detail for our finance team and procurement.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Head of Platform Integrations | Swift Retail
Aisha: +1 415-555-0192

Attachment: swift_june_invoice_0615-0630.pdf (pdf)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@swiftretail.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on June pilot invoice — rounding and long-context requests

Hi Aisha — thanks for the note and attaching the invoice. I've reviewed the invoice and reproduced the line calculations; summary and examples below to map back to your internal logs.

Short answer: the invoice's "token units" are our billing units (post-aggregation/quantum). They do not equal raw model tokens 1:1 because we: (1) apply per-request bundling for very short calls, (2) bucket streaming microcalls into a 50-token quantum for this pilot, and (3) apply a per-call minimum (floor) of 25 token units to avoid extremely high per-call overhead. For long-context sessions the effective unit can be larger because we bill the max sequence length used by the call group after context stitching.

Worked examples (from the invoice rows you flagged):

- Row 3 (conversation id CR-442):
  • Raw model tokens (from your logs): 1,010 tokens (prompt+response).
  • Our batching/roundup: we apply a 10% safety headroom for tokenization variance (1,010 * 1.10 = 1,111).
  • Quantum rounding: we round up to the nearest 10 token units for aggregated rows under the pilot (-> 1,120).
  • Then we coalesce repeated microcalls (3 small requests in the same 30s window) into a single metered group; that grouping increased the billed unit to 1,240 because two additional compressed prefixes were retained in KV cache and charged once per group.
  • Final billed token units: 1,240.

- Long chat surge (6/21 14:35 PDT):
  • These were multi-turn sessions where the active sequence length hit ~42k tokens for a subset of requests. For 64k models we apply context stitching — we bill the peak context length per stitch group rather than per-turn, and we do not amortize across unconstrained prefix reuse. That means a single very long session can show as a large spike on the invoice.

- Rounding / per-call floor:
  • Pilot quantum: 50 token units for streaming microcalls (this is a pilot-specific config that reduces per-token overhead but increases rounding).
  • Per-call floor: minimum 25 token units (applies to non-streaming short calls).

I attached a short spreadsheet with two worked calculations that map a few of your raw logs into our billed rows (token_context_calc_examples.xlsx).

Next steps: if you'd like, we can run a one-off reconciliation script that ingests your raw logs and shows a side-by-side (raw tokens vs billed units) for June; that typically resolves most questions for finance teams. If you'd prefer we can also propose a temporary concession on the rounding quantum for the pilot to reduce friction.

CC'ing Karthik who owns pilot pricing and Jordan who ran the technical onboarding.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 650-555-0107

Attachments: token_context_calc_examples.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>

Karthik — forwarding Aisha's questions and Grace's breakdown. Finance is already getting antsy on their side. My read: we should offer a one-time smoothing concession for June that credits rounding differences >10% of the billed amount (or a fixed credit of $X). That will keep the account warm and simplify procurement.

Suggested ask: can we offer a 20% reduction on rounding inflation for the pilot months (Jun/Jul) capped at $5k as a one-time credit? If yes, I can communicate this to Aisha and loop in legal for SOW amendment.

Grace — do you have the reconciliation script ready to run if they accept?

-Jordan

Conditions: Swift must accept in writing and we will issue the credit on the next invoice cycle; legal should prepare a brief amendment to the MSA specifying the cap and the months covered.

Grace — please attach the reconciliation output and the concession letter once you send to the customer.

-Karthik

Subject: Re: Question on June pilot invoice — rounding and long-context requests

Hi Aisha — quick update and next steps.

1) Reconciliation: I've run the reconciliation against the raw logs you provided. Attached is a side-by-side export that maps each billed row to your raw token counts and shows the exact transforms (headroom, quantum rounding, grouping).

2) Concession: Per Karthik's approval, Redwood will apply a one-time credit that reduces rounding inflation by 20% for June and July 2027, capped at $5,000. That credit will be applied to your next invoice once we receive written acceptance from Swift.

3) Legal & sign: I've attached a one-page concession letter for signature (concession-letter-swift.pdf) and included a DocuSign link for the SOW amendment in the related links above. Once signed we will issue the credit and update the invoice record.

If this works for you, please reply to confirm and I'll route the concession to our finance/legal teams for processing. Happy to schedule a 20-minute call if you want to walk through the reconciliation line-by-line.

Thanks,
Grace
